overview: Launched, scaled and rebuilt WooCommerce research peptide storefronts in a category that Meta, TikTok, Mailchimp, Klaviyo and even WooCommerce's own extensions refuse to serve.

heroMetrics.label: Revenue in a single month on $70K in ad spend
Google Performance Max ROAS across 956 conversions

results.label: Return on total ad spend in the peak month
Google Ads conversion value in 59 days
WooCommerce extensions replaced in under 3 weeks
Share of revenue from a new affiliate channel in its first 30 days

challenge: Research peptides sit in one of the most restricted ad categories online. In the first months the brand lost one platform after another: WooCommerce's parent company dropped support for its shipping, product feed and automation extensions; Mailchimp and Klaviyo closed its email accounts; the Meta ad account was disabled; and TikTok suspended the account the day its first ad went live. Later, a payment processor shut off and conversion tracking stopped reporting sales to the ad platforms. The business had to keep selling through all of it.

approach.heading: Launch on the channels that stay open
approach.body: We set up analytics, Google Ads, Merchant Center, Meta, Instagram and X from scratch in December 2024, then put the budget behind Google Performance Max once it proved it could serve the catalog. As ROAS held, we scaled daily spend to $1,000 and then $1,500. At its peak the store did $230K in revenue in one month on $70K in ad spend.

approach.heading: Rebuild the stack when platforms walk away
approach.body: When the WooCommerce extensions were pulled with a February 22 deadline, we sourced and installed replacements for all seven (UPS and USPS shipping, the Google product feed, cart recovery automation and more) before the cutoff. When Mailchimp and Klaviyo blocked the account, we moved email onto a self-hosted system the business controls.

approach.heading: Tracking that survives change
approach.body: Payment processors changed often, and each change broke purchase tracking. We rebuilt it server side, so every paid order reports to Google Ads, Microsoft Ads and X no matter which processor took the payment. A nightly offline upload recovered $2,315 in Google-driven revenue in its first week that the ad account had never seen. We also fixed the product feed itself: categories mapped to "Hardware" and missing brand and identifier fields on every product.

approach.heading: Channels no platform can shut off
approach.body: We built an affiliate program with a tracked link, partner terms and commission tiers. Partners are paid only on real sales, and in its first 30 days the program produced 24% of revenue at zero media cost. On X, a same-day, same-audience test showed that adding a discount line cut cost per click from $1.14 to $0.86, and X's algorithm then put 2.5 times the spend behind that version.

overview: A rebuilt WordPress website, brand messaging, Google and Meta ads, lead funnels and CRM integration for a red-light body contouring studio, so every inquiry lands in one system with its source attached.

heroMetrics.label: Leads captured and tracked in the first 11 months
Of leads tied to the ad, keyword or channel that produced them

results.label: Landing pages built for each ad platform, Google and Meta
Part nurture sequence for leads who haven't booked
Emails matched to live radio reads, June and July 2026
Day Open House funnel: RSVP page, lead form, 7 emails, 5 texts

challenge: The studio had a strong offer but its marketing ran on tools that didn't talk to each other. Inquiries came in by web form, phone, walk-in and radio. The client database, the email platform and the ad accounts each held part of the picture, and no one could see where a client first came from.

approach.heading: Brand messaging and offer
approach.body: We rebuilt the brand messaging around one clear entry point: a $99 first session with a guarantee of 2 inches lost across six measurements on the first visit, or the session is free. The voice speaks to women 35 to 65 in the Nashville area, including clients dealing with loose skin after GLP-1 weight loss, and a 10-month promotion calendar keeps the offer fresh by season.

approach.heading: Website, landing pages and paid media
approach.body: We rebuilt the website in WordPress with appointment setting and a blog that explains the red-light technology in plain language. We manage Google Ads and Meta ads, each pointing to its own landing page with source capture on every form, so we can see which keyword, ad and age group produces real inquiries and move budget weekly. Event pages, like the Open House RSVP page, follow the same pattern.

approach.heading: CRM integration
approach.body: We connected the studio's customer database to its email and SMS platform, so every segment carries the client's program, referral source and campaign type, down to which radio host's read brought them in. Web and ad leads flow into the same tracker with their channel, keyword or ad name, and landing page attached.

approach.heading: Funnels that run on their own
approach.body: An 8-part nurture sequence answers the reasons people put off booking. Every live radio read has a matching email with the same topic and offer. For the July 2026 Open House we built a 12-day funnel: a Facebook lead form, an RSVP page, 7 emails and 5 texts. An automated workflow turns new red-light therapy research into blog and social drafts.

overview: Patient recruitment for a multi-study research site, with every new patient tagged to the channel that brought them in.

challenge: A research site lives on enrollment, and each study has its own eligibility rules, age limits and deadline. Health-ad rules limit what recruitment ads can say, and outside recruitment vendors charge per referral. The site needed a steady flow of patients it didn't have to rent.

approach.heading: Make organic search the base
approach.body: We manage the site's SEO so people searching for paid studies and conditions near them find the site directly. In 2023 organic search brought in more new patients than the largest outside recruitment vendor and every ad channel combined.

approach.heading: Text the people who already know you
approach.body: Targeted SMS to the existing patient list, one study at a time: COVID-19 (47 new patients), eczema (23) and hypothyroidism (16). It is the lowest-cost enrollment channel a site has.

approach.heading: Paid campaigns built per study
approach.body: Facebook, Instagram and Google Ads campaigns built around one study each, with plain-language qualifying questions written to platform health-ad rules. Monthly content calendars keep every active study visible.

approach.heading: Source tracking end to end
approach.body: Every new patient record carries the campaign that produced it, so the team knows which channel fills which study and where to spend next.

overview: SEO, paid search, HubSpot automation and AI search visibility for a national network of community-based early-phase oncology trial sites.

heroMetrics.label: Ahrefs Domain Rating, October 2024 to October 2026
New referring domains in two years

results.label: More estimated monthly organic visits than two years ago, per Ahrefs
New top-3 Google rankings (53 today, up from 12)
AI automations and workflows configured in HubSpot and beyond
Of email "opens" traced to security bots, so lead scoring was rebuilt

challenge: The network needed to reach two very different buyers: biotech and pharma sponsors choosing where to place trials, and physicians and patients looking for a trial near them. The site had little search authority, email reporting looked healthy but sales activity didn't match it, and AI search engines barely knew the network existed beyond "clinical trials near [city]."

approach.heading: Search authority from the ground up
approach.body: We built the network's SEO program from a Domain Rating of 10 in October 2024 to 34 today, adding more than 1,100 referring domains along the way. The homepage, investigator profiles and phase pages now rank on their own, and the site holds 53 top-3 Google positions, up from 12. Estimated organic traffic grew by about 1,300 monthly visits over the same period. Three Google Ads campaigns, launched in November 2024, cover brand and trials, Performance Max and preclinical research, with form fills reporting back into HubSpot.

approach.heading: Fixing what the email numbers meant
approach.body: HubSpot's own bot filter flagged 66% to 82% of unique opens on broad physician sends. Opens were measuring email security gateways, not doctors. We took opens out of lead scoring, scored on actions a person has to take, such as visiting trial pages, and built a deliverability plan for physician inboxes.

approach.heading: Automation the sales team actually uses
approach.body: More than 10 AI automations and workflows now run across marketing and sales. One example: a HubSpot build turns buying signals such as new funding or partnerships into a single email from the account's sales rep. Five signals, five lists, five templates and five workflows, one build serving the whole team.

approach.heading: AI search visibility, the next frontier
approach.body: We tested real sponsor and patient questions across Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity. The network earns citations on location searches but not yet on tumor type, drug or topic searches. The cause: the trial finder holds 847 URLs in its sitemap and none of them are in Google's index. Getting those pages indexed is the current milestone.

overview: Brand revamp, an expanded website, CRM and LinkedIn outbound for a startup that turns parking garage columns into ad space and protects them at the same time.

Qualified leads at the booth in a day and a half at the National Parking Association convention

results.label: Connection acceptance rate from Atlanta parking operators, with a 10.7% reply rate
LinkedIn outbound campaigns, each built for one buyer type
Convention attendees loaded, tagged and sequenced in the CRM before the show

challenge: The company sells something most buyers have never considered: advertising on parking garage columns that also protects the concrete. That means selling to parking operators, property managers, developers, hotels and advertisers at once, each with a different reason to care, with a two-person founding team and no marketing department.

approach.heading: Brand revamp
approach.body: We rebuilt the brand around what each buyer gets: ancillary revenue for property owners, column and vehicle protection for operators, and minutes of attention for advertisers. That message now carries the website, sales sheets, conference banners and every post.

approach.heading: An expanded website
approach.body: We grew the site with pages for advertisers and for asset and vehicle protection, location content for Chicago and Las Vegas, and eight long-form articles that answer the questions buyers ask before they take a meeting.

approach.heading: A CRM the founders actually use
approach.body: We connected Insightly with separate paths for cold leads and engaged contacts, automatic email capture, and journeys that move people from first touch to conversation without manual follow-up. A 1,700-contact follow-up journey and a 5-email nurture series run on it, with each email linking to a tracked article on the site.

approach.heading: Outbound and conference engine
approach.body: We have run 20 Dripify campaigns on LinkedIn, each aimed at one buyer: parking operators, hotel brands, malls, mixed-use developers, media buyers, out-of-home ad companies, architects, realtors and car rental companies. More than 1,100 decision-makers have accepted the connection, and the best-performing audience, Atlanta parking operators, accepted at 46.5% and replied at 10.7%. For the National Parking Association convention we loaded and tagged 847 pre-registered attendees in the CRM and sequenced outreach before the doors opened. At the convention, the booth logged 40 qualified leads in a day and a half.

approach.body: A dashboard and final report on registrations, white paper downloads, email and social, delivered in early December. Results will be added here once the campaign closes.
